body.name: Sparse switching acquisition certificate \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}\)
body.construction:
A sparse switching certificate \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}\) is a lexicographically ordered finite list of sparse switching records.  Every canonical branch index \(1,\ldots,M\) occurs in exactly one nonempty record.  For such a record, the decoded \(S\) lies in \(\Pi\), \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}(S)\) returns a law handle and exact support table, \(\ell\) names a well-typed slice whose used conditioning event has positive mass, \(T\) is a measured-ancestry single-district source factor extracted from that slice, and \(\tau\) succeeds for the one named branch.  Index-zero records are only paid-protocol markers and contribute no source triple to \(\mathcal R(E_{\mathrm{sw}})\).  Records sharing one protocol pay for it once.  If \(r=|E_{\mathrm{sw}}|\), the record count is prefixed by the Elias-gamma code for \(r+1\), of length \(2\lfloor\log_2(r+1)\rfloor+1\), and every nonempty transcript is self-delimiting.  Consequently the exact length is
\[
 N_{\mathrm{sw}}
 =2\lfloor\log_2(r+1)\rfloor+1
  +\sum_{R\in E_{\mathrm{sw}}}
   \left(|\mathcal A|+|\mathrm{LIT}|+q_M+|V|(1+|\mathrm{LIT}|)
   +\mathbf 1\{b_{\alpha}(R)>0\}|\operatorname{enc}(\tau_R)|\right).
\]
 A certificate is canonical relative to a specified witness universe when it has no index-zero record and uses the canonical successful transcript and the lexicographically first successful protocol--slice--source witness in that universe subject to its represented protocol set.  The optimizer uses the full enumerated witness universe.
